SeverityFix before orderingWhat to do
critical10 place(s) where copper of different nets touches
Fix the routing (run KiCad DRC).
critical1 track segment(s) below the 0.127 mm fab minimum
Widen tracks to at least 0.159 mm where space allows, or choose a fab profile that supports them.
critical1 via(s) with drill below 0.30 mm
Increase via drill to >= 0.30 mm or order an HDI process.
critical1 resistor(s) over their derated power
R4		Use a larger package/higher rating, or a higher resistance.
major1 copper item(s) closer than 0.30 mm to the board edge
Pull copper back to >= 0.38 mm from Edge.Cuts or ask the fab for edge plating.
majorBoard is finer than Eurocircuits supports (pattern)
Widen the listed features, or choose a finer process or another class system.
major1 feature(s) break Eurocircuits process limits
These limits apply to every class of Eurocircuits pattern + drill classes.
major1 via(s) with annular ring below 0.100 mm
Increase via pad diameter (size - drill >= 0.25 mm).

1 · Build the test fixture

Fixture PCB with pogo pins (render of the generated .kicad_pcb)
Probe points on the board (red = supply, dark = GND, green = measured)

Parts

  • 8 x pogo pin P75 (4 crown tip, 4 spear tip)
  • 8 x receptacle R75 (fixture drill 1.40 mm)
  • 0805 resistors: 1 x 1800 ohm, 1 x 8200 ohm, 3 x 10000 ohm, 1 x 33000 ohm, 2 x 82000 ohm, 2 x 100000 ohm
  • 1 x pin header 2 x 4, 2.54 mm; 1 x 2-pin 5.08 mm terminal block
  • 1 x nest (print, PETG)
  • 4 x M3 hex standoff, female-female, 15 mm
  • 4 x M3 x 6 screw + M3 large washer (DIN 9021, 9 mm), on top of each standoff
  • 4 x M3 x 6 screw + M3 nylon washer, standoff to fixture board (from below)
  • 4 x compression spring, outer 8 mm, wire 0.5 mm, free length 10 mm (solid 3.5 mm or less)
  • 1 x vertical toggle clamp, about 25 kg, flanged base (e.g. GH-101-A)
  • 1 x clamp adapter (print)
  • 1 x press plate (print)
  • 4 x M4 x 12 screw + M4 nut, clamp to adapter (nuts in the adapter's channels)
  • 4 x M3 x 10 screw + M3 nylon washer, adapter to fixture board from below (cuts its own thread)
  • 2 x nut + washer for the clamp's spindle, one each side of the press plate
  • 4 x M3 standoffs under the fixture board
1
sample_sensor-fixture.kicad_pcb: Routed by PCB TestKit (26 connections, 11 vias, KiCad's default rules): open it in KiCad, run DRC and order it.
2
Press the receptacles into the plated holes and solder them; insert the pogo pins (crown tips on through-hole leads, spear tips on flat pads - see the probes CSV).
3
Build a nest and a clamp for every board (section below): standoffs, springs, the printed nest, the clamp on its adapter and the press plate. Mount the fixture on M3 standoffs.
4
Solder the divider resistors, header and power terminal. Wire the header to the measurement hardware as shown below.

Wiring

Board nest and clamp (one per board)

The board slides in from the front: it rests on two ledges along its edges, 1.8 mm above the pogo tips, between two rails up to the end stop. Lay it on the rails' lead-in in front of its place and slide it back to the stop. The nest floats on four sprung standoffs: closing the clamp pushes board and nest down 3.3 mm, the pins come up through the open middle of the nest and are compressed 1.5 mm.

The gap above the tips clears J3 on the board's underside while it slides in.

Nest (print with the flat side down)
Press plate (print fingers up)
Clamp adapter (print upside down)
a
Print the parts below (PETG holds its shape under the spring and clamp load), one of each.
b
Screw the 15 mm M3 standoffs onto the fixture board from below (the four NEST holes of every board). Slip a spring over each standoff.
c
Lay the nest on the springs with its bosses over the standoffs and screw a large washer on top of each: the springs lift the nest against the washers, 7.3 mm above the fixture.
d
Put the M4 nuts in the channels under the clamp adapter, bolt the toggle clamp onto it (the cross slots take base patterns within 4 mm of 20 x 16 mm; set fixture.nest.clamp_holes_mm for yours and reprint only the adapter), and screw the adapter to the fixture from below (the CLAMP holes).
e
Take the rubber tip off the clamp's spindle and fix the press plate in its slot with a nut on each side, fingers down, centred over the board.
f
Adjust the spindle: with a board in the nest, the clamp should lock just as the nest reaches the bottom of its travel (3.3 mm down). The fingers then press the board 1.5 mm onto the pins.

2 · Run a production test

Slide the board in along the rails to the stop: it rides above the pogo tips...
...and close its clamp: the board and nest go down, every pogo pin touches its test point
1
Copy the runner folder to the Raspberry Pi and describe your wiring in hardware.json.
2
Once, with known-good boards: python3 pcbtest_runner.py learn --units 3 to fill in signal limits.
3
For every board: slide it into its nest up to the stop, close the clamp, run python3 pcbtest_runner.py test --loop and enter the serial number.
4
Green PASS: next board. Red FAIL: the failed checks are listed and stored in results/results.csv.
StepWhat is checked
S1 Visual inspectionPolarity/orientation correct, IC pin-1 orientation matches silkscreen, Through-hole joints filled, leads clipped <= 1.5 mm, No solder bridges on fine-pitch parts, No cracked MLCCs near the board edge
S2 Unpowered short check (rails to GND)VIN_12V 100.0.., +3V3 100.0.., +5V 100.0..
S3 Apply power (VIN_12V = 12.0 V)VIN_12V 11.4..12.6
S4 Rail voltages+3V3 3.135..3.465, +5V 4.75..5.25
S5 Signal levels (idle)SDA None..None, SCL None..None
S9 Remove power

Production timing

A batch of 1 takes about 29 s to test (29 s per board), and about 1 min 48 s to hand-solder with the jigs (5 parts, 13 joints per board, 1 jig load). Per board, everything together: 2 min 16 s.

Past 1 boards per batch a bigger batch saves less than 5% per board. Estimates (programming 30 s per board, set your own durations in timing in pcbtestkit.json); the runner records the real ones in every result file.

3 · Hand-solder with the jigs

Build order

PassWhatJig
1reflow the 1 SMD part(s) on the bottom side
2reflow the 16 SMD part(s) on the top sidepaste-print nest
3hand-solder J3, U1, C1, C2, J2 (top side)jig set

Paste-print nest for the top side (pass 2)

The top side is printed after the other side has been reflowed. Print sample_sensor-paste-nest-top.stl, put the PCB in it top side up: its parts on the underside sit in pockets, the board lies flat and the frame around it is flush with the board, so the stencil lies flat for printing the paste. PLA or PETG: the nest does not go into the reflow oven.

Paste-print nest (90.25 x 75.25 x 4.9 mm)

Top-side parts

3D-printed jig (66.75 x 51.75 x 24.38 mm)
place part hereclearance for assembled partsalignment post

Print sample_sensor-jig.stl as it is (pockets face up, no supports): PLA or PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 walls. The pocket map is the jig as it lies on your desk.

Fit check passed. The jigs are cut to every part's 3D shape (KiCad's 3D export); the check compares each part with each jig. jig-fit-check/ has the board and every jig in its working position, in KiCad's 3D coordinates: open them together in any STL viewer.
  • top side: Fit check (26 parts, their 3D shapes): nothing touches on the way in; all 5 hand-soldered parts touch their pockets (or their inserts) as the board lands on the support (within 0.01 mm) and are held on all four sides (0.19 to 0.41 mm of play, inserts in place); held by the part beside it, too close for a jig wall between them: C1 -x against U1 (0.19 mm), U1 +x against C1 (1.19 mm); room for inserts: U1 1.0 mm; the holding jig closes over the placement jig without touching it. Estimated (box) shapes: J1, TP1, TP2, TP3, TP4.
  • paste nest, top: Fit check (1 part, their 3D shapes): the board lies flat on the nest and no part touches it.
1
Print both jigs as they are (no supports): sample_sensor-jig-placement.stl (placement jig) and sample_sensor-jig.stl (holding jig).
The two printed jigs: placement jig (left) and holding jig (right)
2
Put the PCB top side up into the placement jig; the stops around the edge locate it.
3
Fit the hand-soldered parts from above, the normal way: C1 (100uF 25V), C2 (47uF 6.3V), J2 (I2C), J3 (12V IN), U1 (LM7805_TO220). Mind polarity marks. The leads go through their holes into the wells under the board; trim leads longer than 10 mm.
PCB top side up in the placement jig; each part goes straight down into its holes
4
Heat: U1 get hot all over while soldered (metal body (to-220)). Line their pockets in the holding jig with 1.0 mm of heat-resistant material (silicone sheet, PTFE or FR-4) so the hot part never touches the print.
5
Put the holding jig on top, pockets down: its posts go through the mounting holes and every part sits in its pocket.
The holding jig comes down over the parts, pockets first
6
Hold both jigs together and turn the stack over. Lift off the placement jig: every lead now points up.
Stack turned over, placement jig lifted off: the board lies in the holding jig, leads up
7
Solder all leads from above, clip them, lift the board out with the finger notches.
Solder from above; the jig holds every part flush and square
Placement jig (72.25 x 57.25 x 13.4 mm): lead wells, post holes and locating stops
